description: Per-cue voice volume multipliers used by the sound manager and sequencer to adjust individual spoken lines relative to global voice settings.

Id.simple: Voice cue name that this volume override applies to.
Id.technical: FName row key. All three AGameSoundManager voice paths ultimately call SoundManager_FindVoiceVolumeRow(DTM+0x7A0, FName(CueName), true, true); PlayVoiceById first obtains that CueName from the VoiceDataTable row. Lookup uses the unsuffixed cue name and happens before GetLocalizedVoiceCueName conditionally appends "_En" (enabled for languages other than Ja/Ko/Zh_Hant/Zh_Hans), so base and <cue>_En playback share one override. The sequencer instead strips one trailing case-insensitive _En from the atom component's cue name before its own finder. Both finders reject None IDs (all sound-manager callers pass bCheckNone=true) and return the first table's matching row; an absent row falls back to multiplier 1.0. The export spells the field ID and contains no None or _En keys.

Volume.simple: Linear multiplier applied to the voice line volume.
Volume.technical: float, constructor default 0.0f, but a null/None lookup is treated as 1.0f and every shipped exported row is 1.3-2.5. It is a linear volume multiplier, not dB and not a 0..1-clamped user setting: values above 1 boost the cue and the table path never clamps them. PlaySystemVoice applies RowVolume * VoiceVolumeB * VoiceVolumeA * (VoiceVolume * MasterVolume); PlayVoice and PlayVoice3DCue call SetVolume with ((VoiceVolume * MasterVolume) * VoiceVolumeA) * (RowVolume * VoiceVolumeB), whose source spelling is selected for the retail /fp:fast multiply tree. Sequencer SetVolume uses CategoryVolume * section Volume * CueVolume, where voice CategoryVolume is VoiceVolumeB * VoiceVolumeA * VoiceVolume * MasterVolume and CueVolume is this row's raw value (or 1.0). Exported values are 1.3-2.5, with two 2.5 rows and one 2.3 row; all others are 1.3-2.0.

notes: Loaded from the VoiceVolumeDataTable primary-asset loader into DTM.VoiceVolumeDataTables (+0x7A0) after all table loads complete; the manager caches only non-null UDataTable pointers. Only one loader is registered for this table, so the export has no shard merge; both generic finders would still return the first table containing a matching row.

Keys use the cue-name namespace consumed from VoiceDataTable.CueName. In the actual export VoiceDataTable.Id also equals CueName for every row, so the two are currently identical, not competing keys; all 1,044 volume IDs match a Voice Id/CueName exactly and each also has a <cue>_En Voice row.

The sound-manager finder itself does not strip _En; it relies on callers passing the unsuffixed source CueName. The sequencer explicitly strips one trailing case-insensitive _En from the atom component's localized cue name before lookup.

A missing row, NAME_None, or an empty table list yields multiplier 1.0f. A present row retaining the constructor's 0.0f would silence the cue, but no exported row is 0 or a sentinel: all 1,044 values are positive and above 1.

The lookup runs only after playback gates: PlaySystemVoice requires bSystemVoiceEnabled; 2D PlayVoice also requires a loaded cue sheet; PlayVoice3DCue requires bVoicePlaybackEnabled, bSystemVoiceEnabled and a loaded cue sheet. Player slot indices and the -1 auto-select handle choose target players only and do not affect row selection.

The read-only export is a single 1,044-row asset with 1,044 unique two-field rows, no blank IDs and no _En keys. All behavior claims come from reconstructed retail C++ with retail RVAs recorded inline; no retail Blueprint reference graph was used and no Blueprint-only reference is asserted. Project AGENTS.md states that retail Blueprints contain no logic.

usages.detail: Resolves the VoiceVolumeDataTable primary asset and caches it in VoiceVolumeDataTables (+0x7A0); helper at line 162 and non-null append at line 146.
Declares the cached FGameDataTableArray VoiceVolumeDataTables at +0x7A0.
Shared typed finder: rejects NAME_None when bCheckNone is true, scans tables in order and returns the first matching FGameDataTableRow_VoiceVolume row.
PlaySystemVoice looks up FName(CueName), defaults to 1.0 and applies the row multiplier before playback; gated by bSystemVoiceEnabled.
2D PlayVoice performs the same lookup after cue-sheet and system-voice gates and sets the player's volume with the four global factors plus the row multiplier.
PlayVoice3DCue, reached from PlayVoice3D at line 1021, repeats the lookup for 3D voice players under its additional bVoicePlaybackEnabled gate.
PlayVoiceById alias: resolves a VoiceDataTables row, then forwards VoiceRow.CueSheetName/CueName to 2D PlayVoice at line 967, which performs the volume lookup.
UpdateLanguageVoiceFlag sets bAppendEnVoiceSuffix at line 304 for languages other than Ja/Ko/Zh_Hant/Zh_Hans; the localization suffix is applied after the volume-row lookup.
System-voice queue cache copies only CueSheetName/CueName from VoiceDataTable rows; Tick replays those cached cue names to PlaySystemVoice at lines 283 and 302.
PlayNextQueuedVoice pops a queued Voice ID, resolves its VoiceDataTable row and calls PlayVoice at line 1196, reaching the same volume lookup.

Sequencer alias path: PlayVoice3D (line 149) and PlayVoice (line 166) resolve a Voice ID through FindSoundRow, call the sound manager with the row's CueName, then apply the per-cue override again in SetVolume.
SetVolume reads GetCueVolume from the atom's cue name and writes CategoryVolume * section Volume * CueVolume; category volume for voice is computed at line 340.
GetCueVolume strips a trailing case-insensitive _En, finds the row in VoiceVolumeDataTables (+0x7A0) through the row-struct-aware finder, and returns the raw value or 1.0.

Sequencer 2D section evaluates a Voice ID and volume into SoundModule.PlayVoice; the 3D evaluator does the same at AbramsSequencerPlayVoice_3DEvaluate.cpp:71 and the unique-pair evaluator at line 554.
Gameplay voice cue forwarded directly to 3D PlayVoice with a character-index player slot; slot choice does not change the cue-name lookup.
Script voice entries call 2D PlayVoice with stored CueSheetName/CueName and a player slot, reaching the shared volume-row finder.
Shikigami controller calls PlayVoice3DCue with the resolved Voice row's CueName and a slot of character index + 6, reaching the same 3D lookup.
